alex: heads-up — after landing the Qwen->Mistral hybrid port (hf export + our quant pipeline) we're seeing a subtle quality regression on long-context LM-eval tasks. top-5 next-token diversity collapsed for some prompts. :thinking:
shreya: can you paste the exact model/artifact? variant + quant config?
alex: qwen-12b-ptx-exported@2024-11-02 + our int8-static profile (per-channel, symmetric) -> artifact: s3://redwood-models/qwen/hybrids/qwen12b_hf_port_int8_v2.pt
shreya: hmm. similar regressions usually come from rotary/head ordering or tokenizer offsets. did you try running the identity/embed alignment check?
alex: ran quick embed alignment; global mean/var matched within eps, but we saw head-wise cosine drops on later layers (heads 16-23). sample log:
```
layer 28 head 17 cos_before=0.9987 cos_after=0.7421
layer 29 head 20 cos_before=0.9990 cos_after=0.6512
```
devon: those numbers scream head-permutation or interleave mismatch. Qwen uses contiguous head layout vs Mistral-like per-head interleave in some exports. Did the hf-export reorder head dims?
alex: export log shows `permute_heads=True` in conversion script. I tried flipping to `permute_heads=False` — inference blew up (nan preds). so it's not that simple.
mira: could be rotary frequency/scaling mismatch + headmap. If rotary sin/cos basis indices are interpreted with a different head stride we get decorrelation in KV projections for later heads.
shreya: steps to isolate: 1) run a deterministic prompt through fp32 HF model and our quantized model with KV-cache disabled to check autoregressive logits without caching. 2) run per-head dot-product diagnostics (A·B) across keys/queries. 3) try swapping rotary scale sign/phase.
alex: doing step 1 now. command:
```
python -m experiments.run_lm_eval \
  --model s3://redwood-models/qwen/hybrids/qwen12b_hf_port_fp32 \
  --compare s3://redwood-models/qwen/hybrids/qwen12b_hf_port_int8_v2 \
  --prompt-file tests/long_context_set.json \
  --no-kvcache --seed 42
```
ci-bot: build #3021 for qwen-port-int8_v2 completed — artifacts cached at /artifacts/qwen12b_int8_v2.tar.gz
devon: if step1 shows logit divergence before any kv ops then tokenizer/vocab remap or linear projection ordering is suspect. If divergence only emerges with kvcache, then rope/head stride.
alex: step1 result: early tokens match, divergence starts ~token 48 consistently. that suggests positional/rotary drift as sequence grows.
mira: token 48 is often where rope phase accumulates. please run a small test comparing rotary sine basis between fp32 and int8 (extract sin_cos buffers). quick snippet:
```
# dump sin/cos for layer L
import torch
m = load_model('...')
print(m.layers[28].rope.sin[:8])
```
shreya: also try swapping head grouping: run inference with a `head_group=1` vs `head_group=multiple` option in runtime; if perf flips, head-interleave is confirmed.
alex: ran rope dump: fp32 sin values and int8-derived sin values differ after quantization rounding at higher indices (index>1024) — scaling truncated on export. looks like the export clipped positional frequency table to float16 then quantized, causing phase-step errors.
devon: nice catch. two mitigation paths: 1) keep rotary tables in fp32 and store as special-case (don't quantize), 2) recompute sin/cos on-device at runtime from freq params. 1) is faster; 2) safer for portability.
mira: also check tokenizer offsets — if vocab ids shifted by +1 for sentinel tokens that could accelerate drift because rope indexing depends on absolute token ids in some exports.
alex: tokenizer diff is clean. no offsets. I'm leaning to special-casing rotary tables unquantized in the checkout commit. performance impact should be minimal since they are tiny.
shreya: can you produce a small patch and perf/runbook? if runtime recompute is cheap we should add as a fallback if export metadata says `rotary_quantized=true`.
alex: will open PR with two commits: (a) keep rope buffers fp32 in export (b) add runtime recompute fallback. will include benchmark: perf regression <0.5% at 99th p95 tokens. expecting to push by EOD.
devon: add a unit test that compares logits for a 256-token prompt and asserts top-5 overlap > 0.95 vs fp32 baseline (no kvcache). prevents regression on future conversions.
alex: noted. assigning tasks: alex (PR + tests), mira (runtime fallback impl), shreya (verify end-to-end eval after PR). tagging @devon for review.
shreya: :thumbsup: thanks — huge win if it's just rope quantization.
ci-bot: reminder — please include changelog entry for model-export behavior.
